title:
Comment of Andrea Rake in Docket(s)/Project(s) P-15423-000
Submission Date: 11/2/2026

documents.name: 152153.txt
documents.text:
Andrea Rake, Anchorage, AK.
As an environmental engineer and Alaska resident, I’m concerned about DeepGreen’s proposal to construct a data center in the Cook Inlet. First, the waste heat from this data center would be absorbed by the Cook Inlet and harm marine ecosystems. The Cook Inlet beluga whales are year-round residents of Cook Inlet and would be negatively impacted if the waters they rely on were damaged by waste heat and noise. These are endangered marine mammals who depend on quiet waterways to communicate, navigate, hunt, and escape predators. 

Additionally, a data center would cause economic harm to our communities that rely on fishing. The Alaska Department of Fish and Game estimates the total value of Upper Cook Inlet commercial salmon fisheries to average $25 million annually over the last three years. Waste heat and noise will damage fisheries, and those effects will increase over time as generations of salmon are impacted.
